report:
Scope of INPUT-10: the human's rulings of 2026-09-26 — Q10 ("how many times do I have to say I don't care about stale indexes and that's a signal to either delete and reindex or just refresh if possible") and its follow-up on the manager's proposal ("yes, lazy auto-reindex on first use") → RG-REQ-001-L06 rewritten (D-STALE-SIGNAL-1; supersedes D-REFRESH-STALE-2 and INPUT-9's INCOMPLETE verdict); Q11 ("pick whatever is easiest and just mark them for opening — 'can't determine — open it and look inside'") → RG-REQ-001-L07 (D-TEST-UNDETERMINED-1) with RG-REQ-010-L06 aligned; Q8 ("option A") → RG-REQ-006-L04's TS clause (D-TS-WORKSPACE-1, superseding IMPORTS-WORKSPACE-PACKAGE-EDGE-1's no-go). Ledger CC-17..CC-19; README queue map. Standalone read-only `codex exec`, evidence inlined (git diff, the three decision records, the rulings verbatim; the reviewer was instructed not to re-litigate the human's substance). Every code claim in a finding was verified on the source before it was applied (routing.rs:206-214; state.rs load_repo → refuse_if_rebuild_interrupted; rebuild.rs sentinel before retire; orchestrator.rs:587-598 NULL extractor for unrouted files). Measurements re-taken on the v0.19.0 witness stores after pass 3.

=== PASS 1 (reviewer gpt-6-sol, text verbatim) ===
1. **L06 asserts an age the comparison cannot establish.** Quote: “When a running version differs from the snapshot's stamp, `orient` and `check` shall render one line beside the index-basis line: `index built by an older rmap (<component> <snapshot_version> → <current_version>[, …]) — run rmap repo rebuild <path>`; a missing or malformed stamp renders `toolchain status unknown (<reason>) — run rmap repo rebuild <path>`.”  
   **Replace with:** “When a running version differs from a complete snapshot stamp, `orient` and `check` shall render one line beside the index-basis line: `index toolchain differs from running rmap (<component> <snapshot_version> → <current_version>[, …]) — run rmap repo rebuild <path>`; a missing, malformed, or structurally incomplete stamp renders `toolchain status unknown (<reason>) — run rmap repo rebuild <path>`.” The current wording is false when the running binary is older than the stamp. The verification criterion should also exercise a structurally incomplete stamp.

2. **L07 conflicts with the catalog’s seed-classification wording.** Quote from RG-REQ-010-L06: “A chunk is test-partitioned by its file's `is_test` or a structural per-symbol marker (Rust `#[test]`/`#[cfg(test)]` on the item or an enclosing module; TS/JS enclosing `describe(`/`it(`/`test(`; Python only with a framework marker); names are never the basis; an unknown partition ranks with production (never demoted) and renders an explicit unknown marker.”  
   **Replace with:** “A chunk is test-partitioned by its file's `is_test` (including the path and filename conventions of RG-REQ-001-L07) or a structural per-symbol marker (Rust `#[test]`/`#[cfg(test)]` on the item or an enclosing module; TS/JS enclosing `describe(`/`it(`/`test(`; Python only with a framework marker); a symbol’s name alone is never the basis; an unknown partition ranks with production (never demoted) and renders an explicit unknown marker.” This preserves the human’s accepted filename conventions without silently contradicting “names are never the basis.”

3. **L07 assigns the repository-wide witness count to one directory.** Quote: “field: poco `Foundation/testsuite/**` flagged test (788 files at v0.19.0), poco `CppUnit/include/CppUnit/Test.h` and leveldb `util/testutil.cc` undetermined.”  
   **Replace with:** “field: poco `**/testsuite/**` flagged test (788 files across poco at v0.19.0), poco `CppUnit/include/CppUnit/Test.h` and leveldb `util/testutil.cc` undetermined.” The inlined measurement gives 788 across poco; RG-REQ-004-L12 separately identifies 281 files under `Foundation/testsuite/`.

4. **L07 omits a catalog consumer that partitions and counts by `is_test`.** Quote: “Every ranked or counted surface that partitions by test status reads it (RG-REQ-007-L03, RG-REQ-009-L01, RG-REQ-010-L06).”  
   **Replace with:** “Every ranked or counted surface that partitions by test status reads it (RG-REQ-004-L12, RG-REQ-007-L03, RG-REQ-009-L01, RG-REQ-010-L06).” RG-REQ-004-L12 explicitly partitions IMPORTS edges by the importing file’s `is_test`; the UNDETERMINED count therefore needs verification on those module surfaces too.

5. **L04 adds the workspace rule without an executable verification criterion for it.** Quote: “**Verification criterion:** `indexer/src/resolver.rs` (`aliased_named_import_uses_imported_name_for_lookup`, `namespace_import_member_resolves_to_target_module`, `default_import_member_does_not_resolve_by_bare_method_name`, `file_resolution_*`, `import_type_only_reads_injected_metadata`, `…malformed_carrier_is_unreadable_not_absent`); Python submodule inference (to be added by PYTHON-SUBMODULE-IMPORT-1): resolver tests for the sibling-module, subpackage, symbol-import (init keeps the target), init-binds-`Y` (init keeps the target) and relative-form cases, each asserting `resolution` and the alternate candidate on the edge; an end-to-end fixture asserting the three targets and `explain <Class>`'s Referenced-by rendering the inferred importers under the inferred remainder.”  
   **Replace with the same criterion followed by:** “TS workspace inference (to be added by TS-WORKSPACE-RESOLUTION-1): a fixture with an indexed workspace `src/index.ts` and an unindexed declared entry shall assert an INFERRED IMPORTS edge, both recorded candidates and the reason on storage read and `imports <file>`; default module views shall exclude and count it, `--include-inferred` shall include it, and the LiveGraph route shall retain and explain its `workspace-local, unedgeable` label; an unrelated bare package shall remain an unresolved external candidate.” This tests option A’s entire stated behavior without extending its scope.

REFINE

=== PASS 2 (reviewer gpt-6-sol, text verbatim) ===
1. **A first request cannot always start the re-index.** The requirement also forbids starting it during a write to that repository or while another repository’s auto-re-index is running. Without a deferred state, that first use can be lost.

   **Quote:** “On the first request for a repository in a daemon process, the daemon compares the running versions with the latest ready snapshot's stamp; when they differ, or the stamp is missing, malformed or structurally incomplete, it starts ONE background FULL index of that repository — a new snapshot, so queries keep serving the previous ready snapshot until the new one is ready (never the in-place `rmap repo rebuild`); at most one such re-index runs at a time across repositories; none starts while an index, refresh or rebuild of that repository is running; a failed re-index is not retried within the process; `RMAP_AUTO_REINDEX=off` disables it.”

   **Replace with:** “On the first request for a repository in a daemon process, the daemon compares the running versions with the latest ready snapshot's stamp. When they differ, or the stamp is missing, malformed or structurally incomplete, it schedules one background FULL index of that repository unless `RMAP_AUTO_REINDEX=off`; the job starts when no index, refresh or rebuild of that repository is running and no other automatic re-index is running, without requiring another request. The full index creates a new snapshot, so queries keep serving the previous ready snapshot until the new one is ready; it never uses the in-place `rmap repo rebuild`. A failed automatic re-index is not retried within the process.”

2. **The queued and failed states cannot be rendered or verified unambiguously as written.** In particular, an unknown stamp and a failed job have two different reasons.

   **Quote:** “In the `check --json` envelope's `value`, `toolchain_staleness` is `{"state":"current"}`, `{"state":"stale","differences":[{"component":<name>,"snapshot_version":<stamped>,"current_version":<running>}, …],"reindex":"running"|"disabled"|"failed"[,"reason":<reason>]}` or `{"state":"unknown","reason":<reason>,"reindex":…}`.”

   **Replace with:** “In the `check --json` envelope's `value`, `toolchain_staleness` is `{"state":"current"}` or has `state` equal to `stale` or `unknown` and `reindex` equal to `queued`, `running`, `disabled` or `failed`. A `stale` value has a non-empty `differences` list of `{"component":<name>,"snapshot_version":<stamped>,"current_version":<running>}` objects; an `unknown` value has `reason` for the unreadable stamp. Either value has `reindex_failure` with the job-failure reason if and only if `reindex` is `failed`.”

   **Quote:** “Until the re-index completes, `orient` and `check` render one line beside the index-basis line: `index toolchain differs from running rmap (<component> <snapshot_version> → <current_version>[, …]) — re-indexing in the background`; when auto re-index is disabled the suffix is `— run rmap repo rebuild <path>`, and when it failed, `— re-index failed (<reason>); run rmap repo rebuild <path>`; an unreadable stamp renders `toolchain status unknown (<reason>)` with the same suffixes.”

   **Replace with:** “While the stamp differs or is unreadable, `orient` and `check` render one line beside the index-basis line. A differing stamp renders `index toolchain differs from running rmap (<component> <snapshot_version> → <current_version>[, …])`; an unreadable stamp renders `toolchain status unknown (<reason>)`. The suffix is `— re-index queued`, `— re-indexing in the background`, `— run rmap repo rebuild <path>` or `— re-index failed (<reason>); run rmap repo rebuild <path>`, according to the re-index state.”

   The L06 verification criterion should correspondingly exercise a first request blocked by each kind of write and by another repository’s re-index, then verify that the queued job starts without a second request.

3. **The final sentence claims more than the requirement guarantees.** Re-extraction is not assured while the job is queued or running, or after opt-out or failure.

   **Quote:** “Toolchain versions are not an invalidation input for refresh; a refresh stamps the running toolchain and does not track facts it copied forward — the first use after an upgrade re-extracts everything, so none survive (human rulings 2026-09-26, D-STALE-SIGNAL-1: "I don't care about stale indexes — that's a signal to either delete and reindex or just refresh if possible"; "yes, lazy auto-reindex on first use").”

   **Replace with:** “Toolchain versions are not an invalidation input for refresh; a refresh stamps the running toolchain and does not track facts it copied forward. When the automatic full index is triggered and completes successfully, it re-extracts the repository into the new ready snapshot (human rulings 2026-09-26, D-STALE-SIGNAL-1: "I don't care about stale indexes — that's a signal to either delete and reindex or just refresh if possible"; "yes, lazy auto-reindex on first use").”

4. **The supersession record leaves the old explicit-rebuild-only ruling apparently active.** CC-17 names D-REFRESH-STALE-2 but not the conflicting remedy in D-REFRESH-STALE-1.

   **Quote:** “## CC-17 (2026-09-26) — RG-REQ-001-L06's toolchain clause had grown, over eight review passes, into a carried-forward provenance mechanism and a `check` verdict the human never asked for → replaced by a lazy automatic background full re-index on the first request after a toolchain change, with one verdict-neutral line while it runs (human rulings, D-STALE-SIGNAL-1; supersedes D-REFRESH-STALE-2; INPUT-10).”

   **Replace with:** “## CC-17 (2026-09-26) — RG-REQ-001-L06's toolchain clause had grown, over eight review passes, into a carried-forward provenance mechanism and a `check` verdict the human never asked for → replaced by a lazy automatic background full re-index on first use, with one verdict-neutral line while it is pending or running (human rulings, D-STALE-SIGNAL-1; supersedes D-REFRESH-STALE-2 and D-REFRESH-STALE-1's explicit-rebuild-only remedy, while retaining its rule that toolchain versions do not invalidate refresh; INPUT-10).”

The four named Pass 1 wording and verification edits are present. These findings concern the rewritten L06 and its decision record, not the substance of the human’s rulings.

REFINE

=== PASS 3 (reviewer gpt-6-sol, text verbatim) ===
1. **The toolchain stamp is described as provenance it does not provide.** Quote: “A snapshot also states which TOOLCHAIN produced it (`toolchain_json`: the per-language extractor versions and the indexer version).” → Replace with: “A snapshot records the toolchain stamp written by its latest full index or refresh (`toolchain_json`: the per-language extractor versions and the indexer version); the stamp does not assert that this toolchain produced every copied-forward fact.” This preserves the human’s accepted refresh behavior without making a false provenance claim.

2. **The rebuild verification cannot use the stated first-load path.** Quote: “a first request arriving during an index, a refresh and a rebuild of that repository, and one arriving while another repository's automatic re-index runs, each render `re-index queued` and the queued job then starts without a second request”. → Replace with: “a first request arriving during an index or refresh of that repository, or while another repository’s automatic re-index runs, renders `re-index queued` and the queued job starts without a second request; a request during `rmap repo rebuild` retains the named rebuilding refusal and queues a post-rebuild stamp check without requiring another request, starting an automatic full index only if the resulting ready stamp differs or is unreadable”. **OBSERVED:** `load_repo` refuses a store bearing the `.rebuilding` sentinel before it can read a ready snapshot (`daemon-runtime/src/state.rs:981–1000`); rebuild writes that sentinel before retiring the store (`daemon-runtime/src/rebuild.rs:268–290`).

3. **L07 calls proposed filename patterns existing routing conventions.** Quote: “`files.is_test` shall be set from the test markers the language defines (Rust `#[cfg(test)]` inclusion chain, C++ gtest markers) and from the per-language path conventions recorded in the routing rules — test directory segments (`test/`, `tests/`, `__tests__/`, `testsuite/`) and test-file names (`.test.`, `.spec.`, `_test.<ext>`, Python `test_*.py`/`*_test.py`); each convention is listed here so adding one is a catalog change.” → Replace with: “`files.is_test` shall be set from the test markers the language defines (Rust `#[cfg(test)]` inclusion chain, C++ gtest markers) and the routing path patterns (`__tests__`, `.test.`, `.spec.`, `test/`, `tests/`), with `testsuite/` added by TEST-EDGE-SCOPE-1A; adding another pattern is a catalog change.” **OBSERVED:** `routing.rs:206–214`, which supplies scanned files’ path-based `is_test`, has neither `_test.<ext>` nor the Python filename patterns (`repo-index/src/scanner.rs:200`).

4. **The workspace exception conflicts with the preceding general rule.** Quote: “a bare-package import emits an IMPORTS edge (unresolved external candidate);” → Replace with: “a bare-package import not covered by the workspace-member rule below emits an IMPORTS edge as an unresolved external candidate;” This makes the ratified INFERRED workspace resolution an explicit exception.

5. **The per-file verification has no named surface.** Quote: “and a per-file answer says ‘test status: can't determine — open it and look inside’.” → Replace with: “and `explain <file>` says ‘test status: can't determine — open it and look inside’.” The existing `explain <file>` surface makes the wording test executable.

REFINE

=== PASS 4 (reviewer gpt-6-sol, text verbatim) ===
1. **RG-REQ-001-L06 evidence overclaims the amended requirement.** Quote: “**Evidence (v0.18.0):** OBSERVED MET.” → Replace with: “**Evidence (v0.18.0):** OBSERVED MET for index-basis and drift reporting only; lazy automatic re-index and its toolchain-status reporting remain unverified.”

2. **RG-REQ-001-L07 evidence does not distinguish the existing fact from the new rule.** Quote: “**Evidence (v0.18.0):** OBSERVED MET as a stored fact; consumed by seeds and surfaces, not yet by complexity ranking (RC-9).” → Replace with: “**Evidence (v0.18.0):** OBSERVED MET for the existing stored `is_test` fact and its seed and surface consumers; `testsuite/` classification, UNDETERMINED marking, and the required wording remain unverified; complexity ranking remains open (RC-9).”

REFINE

=== PASS 5 (reviewer gpt-6-sol, text verbatim) ===
1. **Human ruling is paraphrased inside quotation marks.** Quote: “When the automatic full index is triggered and completes successfully, it re-extracts the repository into the new ready snapshot (human rulings 2026-09-26, D-STALE-SIGNAL-1: "I don't care about stale indexes — that's a signal to either delete and reindex or just refresh if possible"; "yes, lazy auto-reindex on first use").”  
   Replace with: “When the automatic full index is triggered and completes successfully, it re-extracts the repository into the new ready snapshot (human rulings 2026-09-26, D-STALE-SIGNAL-1: "how many times do I have to say I don't care about stale indexes and that's a signal to either delete and reindex or just refresh if possible"; "yes, lazy auto-reindex on first use").”

2. **The decision record overstates per-file provenance.** Quote: “Raised: 2026-09-24 by the manager (rulings page Q10) after verifying that every file and edge row already records its producing extractor (`file_versions.extractor`, `edges.extractor`), which made the ratified carried-forward design (D-REFRESH-STALE-2) a second, coarser copy of existing provenance.”  
   Replace with: “Raised: 2026-09-24 by the manager (rulings page Q10) after verifying that extracted file versions record their producing extractor in `file_versions.extractor` and edges record one in `edges.extractor`; unrouted skipped file versions can have a NULL extractor. The ratified carried-forward design (D-REFRESH-STALE-2) would duplicate the recorded provenance more coarsely.” **OBSERVED:** `file_versions.extractor` is nullable, and the unrouted path assigns `None` (`001-initial.sql:64`; `orchestrator.rs:587–598`).

3. **The test-word boundary is not precise enough to verify the recorded `TestCaller.h` witness.** Quote: “A file whose path carries a test word (`test`, `tests`, `testing`, `tester`, `testutil`) as a whole word but matches no convention and no marker (a test helper, a test framework's own headers, a test utility shipped in a production package) is test status UNDETERMINED (RG-REQ-002-L11): it stays in the production partition, surfaces that partition by test status state the count ("N files whose test status can't be determined — open them and look inside"), and `explain <file>` says "test status: can't determine — open it and look inside".”  
   Replace with: “A file whose path contains `test`, `tests`, `testing`, `tester`, or `testutil` as a case-insensitive token separated by `/`, `.`, `_`, `-`, or a CamelCase boundary (so `TestCaller.h` qualifies), but matches no listed convention or marker, has test status UNDETERMINED (RG-REQ-002-L11): it stays in the production partition, surfaces that partition by test status state the count ("N files whose test status can't be determined — open them and look inside"), and `explain <file>` says "test status: can't determine — open it and look inside".”

REFINE
